title: Palsgraf v. Long Island Railroad — case on appeal (record of trial and proceedings)
provenance: New York State Courts Law Library references this Berkeley-hosted digitization. Selected page assertions below were manually checked against the scanned page images.
caution: 1927 witness testimony is an assertion under oath, not independently established truth. Pleading allegations are claims, not adjudicated facts. In-world dialogue is always simulated.

extracts.text: The record reports service of the summons on October 2, 1924, service of the complaint on November 14, 1924, and service of the answer on December 3, 1924.

The complaint alleges that the railroad owed duties concerning passenger safety, platform crowding, employee control, and combustible substances. These are plaintiff's allegations, not proven factual findings.
Trial proceedings are dated May 25, 1927, in Kings County. Helen Palsgraf was sworn as a witness. The printed record names Matthew W. Wood for plaintiff and Joseph F. Keany for defendant.

Palsgraf testified that she traveled with daughters Elizabeth and Lillian toward Rockaway Beach, bought tickets at East New York, and observed a large crowd on the platform. These statements are attributed testimony.

extracts.section: Helen Palsgraf — the scales and explosion
extracts.text: Palsgraf testified she heard an explosion and firecracker-like noise; she described flying glass, smoke, and platform scales striking her. This is her reported account, not independent proof of every detail.
Palsgraf testified about seeking help for her daughters and being examined by an ambulance doctor; she said she did not know the name of a later railroad doctor who examined her.
